rfi.title: Ten years after Gabon’s post-election violence, painful questions remain
rfi.description: Ten years on, victims of violence that followed president Ali Bongo’s disputed re-election in Gabon are still demanding truth and justice. Questions also remain over the possible involvement of French nationals and the response of the French authorities.

rfi.title: Niger coup attempt: 'Russians saved the day' analyst tells RFI
rfi.description: Niger’s military government has survived its most serious internal challenge since seizing power in 2023, after Russian paramilitaries helped loyalist forces crush last Saturday's attempted coup in the capital, Niamey. RFI spoke to an expert who explains how this episode has left General Abdourahamane Tiani’s junta weakened and more dependent on Russia.

rfi.title: France's international photojournalism festival founder Leroy dies aged 69
rfi.description: Tributes have been pouring in for Jean-François Leroy, the founder of the Visa pour l'image photojournalism festival, who died on Monday at the age of 69.

rfi.title: French high schools scramble to work out rules as phone ban takes effect
rfi.description: The new school year starts on Tuesday in France, and with it comes a new rule: mobile phones will no longer be allowed in high schools. The ban came into force a week before the first day of term, leaving schools with little time to work out how to put it into practice.

rfi.title: UN committee presents legal case for broad slavery reparations
rfi.description: Countries are "legally obliged" to provide broad reparations for harms resulting from both direct and indirect involvement in the transatlantic African slave trade, a United Nations committee has said. This comes amid a fresh interpretation of a global accord, published on Monday.

rfi.title: What the SDF’s dissolution means for Syria’s Kurds and neighbouring Turkey
rfi.description: Nearly a week after the Syrian Democratic Forces agreed to dissolve, the consequences are beginning to take shape for Syria's Kurds and neighbouring Turkey. As the former US-backed force is absorbed into the Syrian state, questions remain over what the country's Kurds have secured in return – from language and political rights to protections for women – and what the end of more than a decade of Kurdish-led autonomy means for Turkey's own conflict with Kurdish militants.

rfi.title: Dissident militia in Colombia says kidnapped French Foreign Legion soldier alive
rfi.description: Colombian rebels have claimed responsibility for kidnapping a Colombian soldier serving in the French Foreign Legion, saying he is alive and in good health nearly a month after he was seized in the south-west of the country. However they warned the government against any military intervention.

rfi.title: EU hides disappointment after Iceland's 'No' vote
rfi.description: The EU put a brave face Sunday on Iceland's vote against restarting membership talks, but the outcome was a bitter pill to swallow – robbing Brussels of a hoped-for success story while delighting its eurosceptic critics.

rfi.title: Fils heads into US Open as leader of the French pack as Djokovic bows out
rfi.description: France's top tennis player Arthur Fils will launch his US Open campaign on Monday in the shadow of a shock first round defeat for the fourth seed and four-time champion Novak Djokovic.

rfi.title: PM Lecornu opens political season as French government returns from summer break
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is bringing his cabinet together on Monday to tackle the increasingly difficult task of drawing up the 2027 budget, with weak growth, rising borrowing costs and the threat of a no-confidence vote narrowing the government’s room for manoeuvre.

rfi.title: French LGBTQ campaigner vows to continue fight after 'despicable' Paris attack
rfi.description: French police officer and LGBTQ rights campaigner Pierre Picavet has vowed to continue fighting discrimination after he was violently attacked outside a bar in Paris this weekend. The suspect of what Paris mayor has described as a "despicable" attack appears in court on Monday.

rfi.title: Macron in Sweden to sign frigate deal, strengthening 'strategic partnership'
rfi.description: Emmanuel Macron will visit Sweden on Monday to sign a €4.3 billion contract for Stockholm's acquisition of four French frigates – a trip that will also provide the French president with an opportunity to discuss broader concerns about European security and NATO cooperation with Sweden's Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson.

rfi.title: Farm workers face a ‘double-edged sword’ of extreme heat and pesticides
rfi.description: As extreme heat makes working outdoors increasingly dangerous, farm workers face another, less visible threat: the pesticides used on the crops around them. Higher temperatures can make these chemicals evaporate faster, increasing workers’ exposure as their bodies are already struggling with the heat.

rfi.title: Zambia's opposition leader charged with treason
rfi.description: Zambia's detained opposition leader Brian Mundubile has been charged with treason, his lawyer said on Sunday, deepening concerns over the government's treatment of political dissent.

rfi.title: Killing of Palestinian children and teens by Israel surges in West Bank
rfi.description: Alia al-Hallaq's son Mohammed was nine when he was killed by an Israeli army bullet last October, but the Palestinian homemaker still speaks of herself as a mother of five, not four.

rfi.title: Women in Zimbabwe push for recognition of 'invisible' domestic labour
rfi.description: In Zimbabwe, women and girls overwhelmingly bear the burden of domestic labour – costing them opportunities outside the home. New policies are being considered to recognise the value of this unpaid work.

rfi.title: Still dancing at 88, Mali’s Mariam Bagayoko keeps tradition alive
rfi.description: At the age of 88, barefoot and cinched into a belt of cowrie shells, renowned singer Mariam Bagayoko still sweeps across the stage with infectious energy, dazzling wide-eyed fans with the rhythms of a bygone Mali.

rfi.title: Guinea-Bissau votes in referendum on giving president more powers
rfi.description: Voters in military-run Guinea-Bissau will cast ballots on Sunday in a referendum that could give the president more powers ahead of a general election meant to restore civilian rule later this year.

euronews.title: France begins new voluntary national service programme
euronews.description: The government's initial aim is to grow the programme to 10,000 volunteers a year, with a long-term goal of up to 50,000 per year in 2035.

euronews.title: Eurasian nations gather in Bishkek to forge stronger ties, new alliances
euronews.description: Heads of 21 global and rising powers gather in Bishkek for the SCO summit as wars strain the global order. China and Russia have previously used the SCO to project their influence and their stand against the West, but the middle powers are now there to seek new economic and political momentum.

euronews.title: Polish prosecutors launch terrorism investigation following fire at drone maker's factory
euronews.description: "As a result of the fire, warehouse facilities were destroyed, and the value of the damage caused amounts to at least 15 million PLN," Polish prosecutors said in a statement.

euronews.title: Magyar says EU must decide whether to 'survive or win' and slams Brussels' lack of leadership
euronews.description: Hungarian PM Péter Magyar told the Bled Strategic Forum that the EU faces a leadership crisis and must make crucial decisions on its future. He also criticised Brussels' daily migration fines against Hungary, calling them unfair despite a 2020 EU court ruling.

euronews.title: Algerian president seeks to impose death penalty on arsonists
euronews.description: Algeria declared three days of mourning after wildfires killed 12 people and injured dozens. Authorities said 46 fires remained active, with 54 people hospitalised for burns, including six in critical condition.

euronews.title: Argentina great Lionel Messi announces retirement from international football
euronews.description: The decision comes shortly after the death of his father, Jorge Messi, which prompted the former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain player to consider his future.

euronews.description: Officials across NATO’s eastern flank say there is no evidence of an imminent Russian attack, even as they strengthen their defences and warn that Moscow’s campaign of sabotage and provocations against Europe is intensifying.

euronews.title: YouTube's new 'exposure-based' model counts hovering over video as a view
euronews.description: YouTube's new "exposure-based model" counts a view from the first frame, across shorts, long-form videos, podcasts and livestreams, inflating creators' headline numbers without changing how much they actually get paid.

euronews.title: New AI models pose growing threat to the global economy, Bailey warns
euronews.description: The Bank of England governor wrote that jurisdictions need to strengthen cybersecurity and enhance preventive measures to correct vulnerabilities that can have a dangerous impact on the global economy.

euronews.title: 'I remain deeply sorry': John Galliano calls off Met Gala retropective show over racism row
euronews.description: Fashion designer John Galliano has apologised again and cancelled a planned retrospective ahead of the annual Met Gala in 2027 amid a growing storm over  racist and antisemitic comments he made in the past.

euronews.title: Germany and France float plan to bring Kallas under von der Leyen's supervision
euronews.description: Under the German-Franco plan, Kaja Kallas would have a more hands-on role inside the European Commission, with broader responsibilities. But Ursula von der Leyen would retain the final say on foreign policy.

euronews.title: South African airline Airlink defends dramatic stadium flyover
euronews.description: Footage of the flyover quickly began circulating on social media, prompting mixed reactions as some expressed concerns over safety.

euronews.title: New finds in the Bernese Jura: meteorite treasure reaches record size
euronews.description: More and more fragments of the Twannberg meteorite are being found in the Bernese Jura; over 2,200 pieces are known and the rare iron meteorite offers rich insights for researchers.

euronews.title: Estonia moves to protect youth’s mental health in the digital age
euronews.description: Estonia joins Europe's youth online-safety push—but chooses expert-led prevention over a blanket social-media ban.

euronews.title: German inflation rises to 2.9% in August, coming in below expectations
euronews.description: Inflation in Germany rose 2.9% in the year to August on the harmonised measure tracked by the European Central Bank, a fresh acceleration from July but well short of the 3.1% economists had expected, in a reading that offers modest relief to policymakers meeting in Frankfurt next week.

euronews.title: 60 years of Notting Hill Carnival: 10 essential songs chosen by its veterans
euronews.description: For London's Notting Hill Carnival’s 60th anniversary, Euronews Culture spoke to 10 people who have helped shape, celebrate and document its culture - asking each of them to choose the one track that, for them, captures the spirit of the biggest festival of its kind in Europe.

lemonde.description: Anton Silouanov a participé, lundi, à une réunion ministérielle du G20 à Asheville, en Caroline du Nord, une première depuis l’invasion russe de l’Ukraine en février 2022. Sa présence a suscité la protestation de plusieurs délégations européennes.

lemonde.title: Au Népal, après les inondations, les glaciologues sidérés par l’ampleur de la catastrophe
lemonde.description: Les scientifiques de ce pays himalayen connaissent le danger représenté par la fonte accélérée des glaciers. Mais aucun n’avait anticipé un effondrement et une crue de cette magnitude.

lemonde.description: Prévu en mai 2027, l’événement devait ouvrir le très médiatisé Met Gala annuel. lemonde.description: Déclarée au mois de mai, la flambée actuelle est la pire de l’histoire du pays. Elle est causée par le variant Bundibugyo, contre laquelle il n’existe ni vaccin ni traitement.

lemonde.description: A 39 ans, l’octuple lauréat du Ballon d’or a annoncé, lundi sur Instagram, mettre fin à sa carrière internationale. Avec l’Argentine, celui qui poursuit en club, à l’Inter Miami, aura remporté une Coupe du monde de football et deux Copa America.

Tennis: Tamara Korpatsch scheidet bei US Open in der ersten Runde aus
zeit.description: Deutschlands derzeit beste Tennisspielerin verliert bei den US Open gleich ihr erstes Match. Erst zur Mitte des zweiten Satzes findet sie ins Spiel.

zeit.title: Cem Özdemir: Özdemir Breaking Bad
zeit.description: Cem Özdemir steigt in den Wahlkampf von Sachsen-Anhalt ein. Und der Grüne agiert härter als zuletzt. Die Favoritenrolle der AfD verändert seinen Auftritt.

zeit.title: Radsport: Pogacar-OP gut verlaufen - WM-Chance nach Horror-Sturz?
Vor der Landtagswahl: Hüskens vermisst Debatten im Wahlkampf
Landtagswahlen: Merz bei erstem Wahlkampfauftritt in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern beschimpft
zeit.description: Bei seinem ersten Termin im Wahlkampf in Ostdeutschland fordern Gegner von Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz dessen Rücktritt. In Sachsen-Anhalt warnt er erneut vor der AfD.

zeit.title: »Luft nach unten«  von Tamara Štajner: Der Körper vergisst nichts
zeit.description: In »Luft nach unten« erzählt Tamara Štajner von einer Musikerin, ihrer zerstörerischen Mutter und den langen Schatten des Balkans.

zeit.title: Angriffe auf Ukrainer in Polen: Sie fürchten die Wut
zeit.description: Polen half nach dem russischen Angriff wie kein anderes Land ukrainischen Geflüchteten. Nun aber nehmen dort Übergriffe auf Ukrainer zu.

zeit.title: Palliativmedizin: »Unsere Kindheit holt uns ein, wenn es ums Sterben geht«
zeit.description: Wie wird es sein zu sterben? Yvonne Petersen hat jahrzehntelang Todkranke begleitet. Am Ende, sagt sie, erkenne man gut die Bindungsmuster, die ein Mensch erlernt hat.

france24fr.title: 🔴 L'ancien Premier ministre Édouard Balladur est mort à l'âge de 97 ans
Mort de l'ancien Premier ministre Édouard Balladur à 97 ans
france24fr.description: Édouard Balladur, Premier ministre entre 1993 et 1995, est mort lundi à 97 ans. Ancien proche de Jacques Chirac, il était devenu son rival lors de la campagne présidentielle de 1995. Son échec au premier tour avait mis fin à ses ambitions nationales.

france24fr.title: Crise au Népal : onde de choc régionale ?
france24fr.description: Au Népal, le bilan des victimes est revu à la hausse chaque jour. Des identifications sont toujours en cours. "Une catastrophe naturelle déchirante",  a jugé le Premier Ministre du Népal Balendra Shah. Plusieurs questions ce soir dans le débat : Comment le Népal gère-t-il les secours ? Quel rôle jouent l'Inde et la Chine ? Quid des Etats-Unis et de l'Europe ? La catastrophe climatique d'aujourd'hui peut-elle dégénérer en une catastrophe humanitaire ? Doit-on s'attendre à une déstabilisation de l

france24fr.title: Niger : le calme revient à Niamey après la mutinerie
france24fr.description: 🇳🇪 Au Niger, le calme est de retour à Niamey, après une nuit de vendredi à samedi marquée par une mutinerie déjouée par le régime militaire. Avec l’appui de ses alliés russes, les paramilitaires d’Africa Corps ont effectué une tournée dans la capitale. Retour en images avec Gaëlle Fonseca.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : l'opposition rejette les consultations annoncées par Tshisekedi
france24fr.description: 🇨🇩 En RDC, le projet de dialogue national de Félix Tshisekedi divise déjà. L’opposition, réunie au sein de la coalition C64 et les partisans de Joseph Kabila, rejette les consultations annoncées. La majorité présidentielle, elle, défend le processus.

france24fr.title: Cameroun : Les migrants expulsés des États-Unis dénoncent leurs conditions
france24fr.description: 🇨🇲 🇺🇸 Le Cameroun fait partie des pays qui auraient conclu un accord secret avec les États-Unis pour accueillir des personnes expulsées. Alors que ces personnes vivent souvent dans des conditions précaires et risquent de subir des persécutions similaires à celles de leur pays d’origine.

france24fr.title: Crue dans le Grand Canyon: le rôle du changement climatique
france24fr.description: Une crue soudaine dans le Grand Canyon a fait au moins 1 mort et 15 disparus. La rivière qui coule dans la Bright Angel Creek a vu son débit multiplié par 20 en un temps très court. Sur le sol aride, donc imperméable, de la zone et à la faveur de pentes très raides, un mur d'eau a fondu sur les randonneurs. Le changement climatique joue un rôle dans l'amplification des averses. Et la rapidité de ces modifications du système climatique rend plus difficile la prévision de ces événements extrêmes.

france24fr.title: Venezuela : Alejandro Betancourt, le sulfureux magnat du pétrole sur lequel Trump veut miser
france24fr.description: En annonçant vendredi avoir conclu un accord avec le Venezuela pour obtenir “65 milliards de barils” de pétrole, Donald Trump avait précisé que Washington travaillerait avec un intermédiaire. Il s’agit d’Alejandro Betancourt, un homme d’affaires controversé qui a fait fortune grâce au chavisme.

france24fr.title: Massachusetts : une nouvelle loi autorise-t-elle l’avortement "jusqu’à l’accouchement" ?
france24fr.description: Depuis l’adoption d’une nouvelle loi sur l’avortement au Massachusetts, plusieurs publications virales sur les réseaux sociaux affirment que l’État autoriserait désormais les interruptions de grossesse jusqu’au jour de la naissance. Qu’en est-il vraiment ?

france24fr.title: The Cure, Interpol, et interdiction de fumer : les temps forts de Rock en Seine
france24fr.description: Sur les cinq jours du festival de Rock en Seine, 175 000 personnes ont répondu présentes malgré les aléas de la météo. Le dernier festival de musique de l'été a fait le plein aux portes de Paris. Retour sur les meilleurs moments.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Lionel Messi annonce qu'il ne jouera plus avec l'Argentine
L'Argentin Lionel Messi annonce sa retraite internationale
france24fr.description: L'attaquant ​argentin Lionel Messi a annoncé ​lundi ‌sur ⁠Instagram ‌sa retraite internationale. Lionel Messi, ⁠39 ans, a guidé ​l'Argentine ‌au titre de championne ‌du monde ​en 2022 mais n'a pu ​empêcher sa ​défaite ​en finale contre ​l'Espagne cette année.

france24fr.title: Guinée : Mamadi Doumbouya sur les lieux de l’éboulement meurtrier à Conakry
france24fr.description: 🇬🇳 En Guinée, une semaine après l’éboulement meurtrier à Conakry, Mamadi Doumbouya s’est rendu sur le site du drame. Le bilan est d’au moins 34 morts, selon les autorités, qui promettent des mesures pour éviter une pareille catastrophe à l'avenir.

france24fr.title: Les États-Unis et le Venezuela annoncent un accord pétrolier "historique"
france24fr.description: Washington et Caracas ont annoncé vendredi avoir conclu un accord pétrolier "historique", qui verra les Etats-Unis prendre le contrôle majoritaire de plus de 65 milliards de barils des réserves du Venezuela. Les explications de Luis Colasante, expert en politique énergétique et spécialiste des marchés d'énergie.

france24fr.title: Pénalisation du port du voile : le RN pousse un marqueur du lepénisme et propose un référendum
france24fr.description: Proposition historique de Marine Le Pen, l'interdiction du port du voile islamique en public est remise sur la table par la candidate du Rassemblement national qui promet, si elle accède à l'Elysée, un référendum qui déboucherait sur une sanction pénale.

france24fr.title: 🇳🇵 Népal : après la crue meurtrière, survivre coûte que coûte
france24fr.description: Après la crue meurtrière du 26 août au Népal, les sinistrés font face au chaos et à l'incertitude. Un reportage de nos envoyés spéciaux Ondine de Gaulle, Shahzaib Wahlah, et Achraf Abid.

france24fr.title: En déployant ses avions de combat au Niger, l'Algérie veut "prévenir d'éventuelles attaques"
france24fr.description: Pour la première fois, l'Algérie a déployé dimanche des avions de combat au Niger après qu'une mutinerie contre la junte a été déjouée la veille à Niamey. Selon le journaliste spécialisé en défense et sécurité Akram Kharief, Alger veut afficher son soutien aux autorités nigériennes et cherche à lutter contre le terrorisme, sans rompre avec sa doctrine de non-intervention à l'étranger.

france24fr.title: Emmanuel Macron à Stockholm pour conclure une importante vente de frégates
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron et le Premier ministre suédois Ulf Kristersson vont signer lundi à Stockholm un contrat de 4,3 milliards d'euros pour la vente par la France de quatre frégates à la Suède qui consacre la coopération militaro-industrielle entre les deux pays, sur fond de menace russe croissante en Europe.

nzz.title: Polizei-Affäre in Uster: Der Gemeinderat will eine parlamentarische Untersuchungskommission einsetzen
nzz.description: Jahrelange Finanztricks, kaum Kommunikation: Nun sollen die Vorkommnisse geprüft werden.

nzz.title: «Es ist kein Sieg für die UBS»: Die Wirtschaftskommission des Ständerates stellt sich beim Eigenkapital gegen die Finanzministerin Keller-Sutter
nzz.description: Nach zähen Verhandlungen spricht sich die vorberatende Kommission für eine grössere Rolle von AT1-Anleihen bei der Kapitalausstattung der UBS aus. Das sind die wichtigsten Eckwerte.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Moskau-Treffen von CIA-Chef habe Ziele erreicht, sagt der Präsident Litauens
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Dies sind die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Jetzt sind auch die besten Schweizer Fussballschiedsrichter Profis – die Liga wirft dafür 700 000 Franken auf
nzz.description: Acht Referees werden zu 80 Prozent fest angestellt. Damit macht der Schweizer Klubfussball einen längst fälligen Schritt der Professionalisierung – sieben Jahre nach der VAR-Einführung.

nzz.title: Lionel Messi tritt aus der argentinischen Nationalmannschaft zurück
nzz.description: Für Argentinien und den Weltfussball beginnt eine neue Zeitrechnung.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Die Privilegien der Beamten sind nicht mehr zeitgemäss – Deutschland muss umdenken
nzz.description: Der Beamtenstatus kostet den deutschen Staat Milliarden – und wurde vom Verfassungsgericht noch einmal betoniert. Ein aktueller Fall zeigt die Schieflage. Höchste Zeit, die Verbeamtung auf das zu beschränken, wofür sie geschaffen wurde.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die Schande vom Lindenhof: Die Zürcher Sicherheitsvorsteherin Karin Rykart hätte die Besetzung des historischen Platzes durch Linksextreme beenden müssen
nzz.description: Bei KMU setzt die Stadt Regeln durch, linken Aktivisten lässt sie freie Hand. Das darf nicht sein. Basel macht vor, wie es anders ginge.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Vontobel-Wegzug ist ein Warnsignal: Die Zürcher Überheblichkeit gefährdet den eigenen Standort
nzz.description: Der Abgang der Vorzeigebank muss Zürich wachrütteln. Das Unbehagen vieler Firmen wächst: Ohne bessere Rahmenbedingungen erodiert die wirtschaftliche Attraktivität von Stadt und Kanton weiter.

nzz.title: Ein Tatverdächtiger gefasst, sein Motiv weiterhin unklar – und das «Sicherheitsgefühl leidet», wie der Stadtpräsident von Aarau sagt
nzz.description: Am zweiten Tag nach der Schiesserei auf dem Schachenareal gibt es weiterhin keine definitive Gewissheit. Die Stadt prüft, wie sich Anlässe der kommenden Tage besser schützen lassen.

nzz.title: Gegen Wokeness und Ukraine-Hilfe: wie Giuseppe Conte die italienische Opposition für sein Comeback erpresst
nzz.description: Nächstes Jahr sind in Italien Wahlen. Vier Jahre nach ihrer Niederlage ringt die Opposition noch immer um Geschlossenheit. Statt an einem gemeinsamen Programm zu arbeiten, kämpfen die Parteiführer um die Macht. Davon profitiert Meloni.

nzz.title: Hübsche Frauen, teurer Champagner, schnelle Kohle: Die ARD macht Escort-Girl zum Traumberuf
nzz.description: Die neue Dramedy «Selling Sex» will weibliches Empowerment zeigen. Was als feministischer Akt gedacht ist, verkommt zum hübsch inszenierten Voyeurismus.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Schweiz: Bund führt biometrische Identitätskarte ein
Temperaturrekorde und Dürre: Warum dieser Sommer in Europa so heiss ist
nzz.description: Durch den Klimawandel sind die Häufigkeit und die Intensität von Hitzewellen gestiegen. Doch er ist nicht der einzige Grund für das extreme Wetter.

nzz.title: Noch 900 Arbeiter von Wasserkraftwerken in Nepal vermisst – Rettungskräfte suchen in Tunneln nach Überlebenden
nzz.description: Die verheerende Sturzflut in dem Himalaja-Tal hat mehrere Staudämme zerstört und unterirdische Kraftwerke geflutet. Für die Regierung von Balen Shah ist die Krise eine ernste Bewährungsprobe.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Tödliche Sturzflut in Nepal: Bilder zeigen die Zerstörung und das Leid
nzz.description: Eine riesige Flutwelle hat im Himalaja mehr als 700 Todesopfer gefordert und ganze Ortschaften fortgerissen. Mehr als 3000 Personen gelten als vermisst.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - «Die Sicherheitsleute haben durch ihr selbstloses Verhalten Schlimmeres verhindert», sagt der Veranstalter des Aarauer Raves
nzz.description: Erstmals äussert sich Olivier Grein, der Leiter der Event-Agentur, die die Techno-Party in Aarau organisiert hat. Er sieht nach der tödlichen Schiesserei die Politik in der Pflicht.

spiegel.title: D4vd: US-Rapper plädiert im Mordfall an 14-Jähriger auf nicht schuldig
spiegel.description: Der 21-jährige Sänger D4vd soll ein junges Mädchen getötet und ihre Leiche zerstückelt haben. Er weist die Vorwürfe erneut zurück. Sein prominentes Anwaltsteam hat nun das Mandat niedergelegt.

spiegel.title: Zürich – Schweiz: Kantonsrat will Kopftücher in Klassenzimmern verbieten
spiegel.description: Die Schweiz streitet über religiöse Symbole in Bildungsstätten. Jetzt hat sich die rechtspopulistische SVP mit einem Anliegen durchgesetzt, Kopftücher an Zürcher Schulen zu verbieten. Beschlossen ist das Verbot noch nicht.

spiegel.title: Alec Baldwin: Warum seine Villa in den Hamptons ein Ladenhüter ist
spiegel.description: Die Lage könnte exklusiver sein, wirkt aber noch traumhaft genug. Vielleicht ist Alec Baldwin selbst der Grund, weshalb er keinen Käufer für sein Haus in den Hamptons findet.

spiegel.title: Nepal: Verschüttete in Wasserkraftwerken – »Immer weniger Hoffnung«
spiegel.description: Rund 900 Arbeiter werden nach der verheerenden Flutkatastrophe allein in nepalesischen Wasserkraftwerken vermisst. Sie werden in den verwüsteten Tunnelsystemen vermutet. Eindrücke von SPIEGEL-Korrespondent Serafin Reiber.

spiegel.title: Sven Schulze im SPIEGEL-Talk: »Siegmund ist eine Marionette«
spiegel.description: Kann Sven Schulze die AfD noch stoppen? Hier spricht Sachsen-Anhalts Ministerpräsident über Druck im Wahlkampf, Fehler seiner CDU – und die Frage, mit wem er nach der Wahl regieren würde.

spiegel.title: Hendrik Holt: Das ist über die Flucht des Windkraftbetrügers und Hochstaplers bekannt
spiegel.description: Er prellte Konzerne um Millionen und ließ sich im offenen Vollzug von einem TV-Team begleiten: Der verurteilte Kriminelle Hendrik Holt ist auf der Flucht. Frau und Kind ließ er offenbar zurück. Der Überblick.

spiegel.title: Kapstadt: Riskantes Flugmanöver vor 55000 Zuschauern – wie gefährlich war der doppelte Flyover in Süsafrika?
spiegel.description: Zwei Passagierjets sind mit winzigem Sicherheitsabstand über ein voll besetztes Stadion in Südafrika hinweg gedonnert. Die Fluggesellschaft zeigt sich begeistert – international sorgt die Aktion für Kopfschütteln.

spiegel.title: Hockey-WM: Kapitän Tom Grambusch über Führungsstil und Teamgeheimnis
spiegel.description: Die deutschen Hockey-Herren sind Weltmeister. Kapitän Tom Grambusch hat das Amt von seinem Bruder übernommen und pflegt einen anderen Führungsstil. Was ist das Geheimnis des Teams?

spiegel.title: VW sieht für Werk in Hannover bislang keine Nachfolgeproduktion – Gewerkschaft gibt sich kampfbereit
spiegel.description: Die Fronten bei Volkswagen sind verhärtet. Tausende Beschäftigte verfolgen eine Sonderversammlung im VW-Werk Hannover. Betriebsrat und IG Metall pochen auf bestehende Zusagen – und erhöhen den Druck.

spiegel.title: BYD, Geely, Xpeng: Germany’s Vaunted Auto Industry in Dire Straits Amid Chinese Surge
spiegel.description: The numbers of Chinese cars on European roads is skyrocketing as carmakers from the People’s Republic rush to build factories in the EU. Germany’s traditional brands are struggling to respond.

spiegel.title: Anschlag in Leipzig: Friedrich Merz will Verantwortliche benennen – und muss mögliche Gegenreaktion einkalkulieren
spiegel.description: Der Kanzler will in den »nächsten Tagen« sagen, wer hinter dem gescheiterten Drohnenanschlag auf dem Leipziger Flughafen steckt. Was auf Russland hindeutet und wie Deutschlands Antwort ausfallen könnte.

spiegel.title: Met-Gala-Ausstellung von Designer John Galliano abgesagt
spiegel.description: Das Metropolitan Museum of Art wollte 2027 John Galliano ehren. Doch es gab Kritik wegen früherer Äußerungen des Designers. Nun wurde die geplante Schau abgesagt.

spiegel.title: Lionel Messi beendet seine Länderspielkarriere und wird nicht mehr für Argentinien spielen
spiegel.description: Es gibt wenige Rekorde, die Lionel Messi im Trikot der argentinischen Nationalmannschaft nicht gebrochen hat. Nach dem verlorenen WM-Finale gegen Spanien soll Schluss sein.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Iran, Wahlkampf mit Merz, Nosferatu-Spinne
spiegel.description: Satellitenbilder zeigen, dass Iran eine mutmaßliche Nuklearanlage wohl bereits repariert. Friedrich Merz steigt in den Wahlkampf in Sachsen-Anhalt ein. Und die Nosferatu-Spinne ist da – nur diesmal ohne Bild. Das ist die Lage am Montagabend.

spiegel.title: Korallenriffe haben kaum noch Zeit zur Erholung – auch wegen Klimaphänomen El Niño
spiegel.description: Es ist die bisher größte globale Bestandsaufnahme: Forschende haben weltweit an Zehntausenden Standorten Korallenriffe untersucht. Ihre Ergebnisse zeigen: Die Riffe sind massiv gefährdet. Aber noch nicht verloren.

spiegel.title: Norwegen: Marius Borg Høiby darf trotz Hausarrest zum Begräbnis von König Harald V.
spiegel.description: Auch wegen zwei Vergewaltigungen sitzt Marius Borg Høiby im königlichen Hausarrest. Für die Trauerfeiern für seinen Ziehopa König Harald V. darf er aber raus.

spiegel.title: Grundsicherung: Union drängt auf Ende der Zahlungen für mit Haftbefehl Gesuchte
spiegel.description: Das Arbeitsministerium will bis Ende des Jahres den Aktionsplan gegen Sozialmissbrauch umsetzen. Der Union geht das zu langsam: Arbeitsministerin Bas habe offenbar keine Eile, wirft ihr Unionsfraktionsvize Krings vor.

spiegel.title: Italien hat laut Prognose zum demographischen Wandel bis 2050 fast vier Millionen weniger Einwohner
spiegel.description: Die Geburtenrate erreicht in Italien neue Tiefstände. In den kommenden Jahrzehnten wird die Bevölkerung Prognosen zufolge um Millionen schrumpfen. Auch Maßnahmen von Ministerpräsidentin Meloni konnten den Trend nicht aufhalten.

observador.title: A Europa pode dar-se ao luxo de se afastar dos EUA?
observador.description: Para Helena Ferro Gouveia, a Europa não deve prescindir da aliança com Washington devido à dependência defensiva e aos valores comuns. Salienta ainda os ataques híbridos da Rússia contra solo europeu.

observador.title: Macbeth, monólogos e teatro no carro: o que ver este mês
observador.description: De norte a sul do país, a rentrée teatral traz espetáculos muito antecipados, entre eles novas criações de Tiago Rodrigues e Sara Barros Leitão. Em Lisboa, reabre o Teatro Nacional D. Maria II.

observador.title: PSD quer esclarecimentos sobre fecho do Hospital Termal
observador.description: A suspensão dos tratamentos no Hospital Termal desde 20 de agosto gerou crise política na câmara. PSD exige saber o que correu mal nas obras ao furo AC2 iniciadas a 5 de agosto.

observador.title: Pinheiro centenário cai e provoca estragos em nove carros
observador.description: A árvore, classificada pelo ICNF, tombou por falência da raiz numa área verde junto à Rua Engenheiro Henri Perron. Não há feridos a registar.

observador.title: As notícias das 20h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Uttar Pradesh. Explosão em fábrica ilegal mata 11
observador.description: A fábrica funcionava ilegalmente em Uttar Pradesh. Modi anunciou 1.800 euros para famílias de cada vítima mortal e apoio aos feridos.

observador.title: O Tribunal Constitucional fragilizou o Presidente?
observador.description: A decisão unânime de validar a Lei do Retorno é um revés político, que retira margem para um futuro veto presidencial. A nova conferência de imprensa vai salvar o ministro da Administração Interna?

observador.title: Taranto2026.  Dongmo e Inchude fazem dobradinha no peso
observador.description: Com 19,42 metros, Auriol Dongmo estabeleceu um novo recorde dos Jogos do Mediterrâneo. Jéssica Inchude ficou em segundo, com 18,86 m.

observador.title: Futebolistas investigados por alegadas ligações a tráfico
observador.description: Quatro detidos, 15 buscas e 100 agentes mobilizados. DVD, avançado do Vasco, e Hayner, do Vila Nova, estão entre os alvos das operações policiais.

observador.title: Cimeira. Modi pede fim da guerra na Ucrânia a Putin
observador.description: O encontro realizou-se à margem da cimeira da Organização de Cooperação de Xangai, no Quirguistão. Negociações de paz promovidas pelos EUA estão paradas.

observador.title: PS questiona exclusão do Algarve de nova áreas empresariais
observador.description: Socialistas interpelam ministro Castro Almeida sobre localizações anunciadas em julho: duas no Norte, duas no Centro, uma em Lisboa e uma no Alentejo. Algarve ficou de fora.

observador.title: Jovem acusado de 76 crimes de pornografia de menores
observador.description: O jovem usou Discord e Telegram para enviar tutoriais de automutilação a raparigas vulneráveis e partilhar conteúdos de abuso sexual de menores.

observador.title: Chega reúne-se para "decisão final" sobre moção de censura
observador.description: O líder do Chega vai reunir-se com a direção nacional e a bancada parlamentar para chegar a uma "decisão final" sobre a moção de censura contra Luís Neves. Ventura pediu uma reunião com Seguro.

observador.title: Homem de 65 anos morreu em colisão na A24 perto de Vila Real
observador.description: Mulher de 60 anos que seguia no mesmo motociclo ficou também gravemente ferida. Acidente aconteceu ao quilómetro 83,800, entre Nogueira e Vila Real.

observador.title: Giménez, "El Bebote" que quer voltar a crescer no Dragão
observador.description: Depois de duas épocas e meia no Feyenoord que o colocaram no radar de várias equipas europeias, experiência no AC Milan falhou. Agora, avançado mexicano de 25 anos aposta nos dragões para "ressurgir".

observador.title: Entrou, serviu, marcou: Mora, o novo príncipe de Roma
observador.description: Num jogo em que Malen voltou a decidir cedo, Mora rendeu Soulé aos 60' e marcou cinco minutos depois o seu primeiro golo na Serie A frente ao Lecce de Tiago Gabriel em mais uma goleada da Roma (0-4).

observador.title: Seguro promulga Lei do Retorno após ter "segurança jurídica"
observador.description: Presidente promulgou Lei do Retorno após ser validada pelo TC. Seguro justifica que lei exigia "segurança jurídica" antes de ser validada e que decisão dos juízes "esclarece dúvidas interpretativas".

observador.title: 19h. PRR. PS quer ouvir ministro da Economia com urgência
observador.description: Castro Almeida anunciou a conclusão do PRR, mas o PS quer saber o “estado efetivo” da execução. Ainda, Adalberto Campos Fernandes rejeita derrota de Seguro após decisão do TC sobre a Lei do Retorno.

letemps.title: «Rochebrune», de Sophie Divry, ou les vacances comme ultime espoir d’un couple qui bat de l’aile
letemps.description:
Qui, de la psyché humaine ou du massif des Hautes Aigues, a le relief le plus escarpé? Dans «Rochebrune», Sophie Divry fait de la vie conjugale un sport extrême

Selon l’Office fédéral de la statistique, en 2021, 6% des enfants vivaient dans une famille recomposée. C’est également le cas de Noémie et de Léon, et dans Rochebrune, Sophie Divry nous raconte les dessous de leur quotidien

letemps.title: Edouard Balladur, premier ministre et rival malheureux de Jacques Chirac à la présidentielle de 1995, est mort à 97 ans
letemps.description:

phys-org.title: Small-plane fuel raises lead levels up to sevenfold near Oregon airports, study suggests
phys-org.description: Emissions from aircraft that use leaded aviation gasoline are a significant source of environmental pollution in neighborhoods near regional airports, according to a new study by researchers at Oregon State University and Portland State University. The findings were published in Communications Sustainability.

phys-org.title: Why atmospheric nanoparticles grow at similar rates everywhere
phys-org.description: Aerosols have a profound influence on air quality, human health, clouds and climate, but new particle formation in the atmosphere has remained a scientific conundrum. Large fractions of airborne fine particulate matter consist of secondary organic aerosols (SOA) formed by gas-to-particle conversion of organic precursor molecules in the atmosphere. The growth rates of these atmospheric nanoparticles, however, have remained enigmatic: They are often smaller and less dependent on condensable vapor

phys-org.title: Why do some proteins accumulate even on protein-resistant surfaces?
phys-org.description: Proteins with exposed arginine can selectively accumulate even on protein-resistant coatings, as reported by researchers from Science Tokyo. Through an in-depth analysis of which proteins adhere and how they adhere to various anti-fouling surfaces, the team found that arginine disrupts the protective water layer that normally blocks adsorption. Their results will help scientists develop safer and more effective biocompatible materials for medical devices, such as stents and advanced biosensors.

phys-org.title: Why some AI ads fail while others succeed
phys-org.description: Artificial intelligence can create realistic depictions of just about anything, but that does not mean advertisers should lean on the technology, according to a study led by University of Mississippi professors.

phys-org.title: Four 'Little Red Dot' pairs hint at black hole mergers in early universe
phys-org.description: After analyzing infrared images captured by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), an international team of researchers has discovered multiple massive black holes from approximately 12.5–12.8 billion years ago that were actively accumulating surrounding matter and growing rapidly. Some were even on the path to merging, according to a study published Aug. 31 in the Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan.

phys-org.title: Peptides can form well-defined structures in harsh, Venus-like conditions
phys-org.description: When exploring solar system bodies for signs of past or present life, scientists have mainly focused on planets that have (or had) a liquid surface similar to Earth's. However, mounting evidence suggests that the ingredients for life may exist in a very different environment: the highly acidic clouds that blanket Venus.

phys-org.title: Loss of kelp forests reverberates down to the microbial level
phys-org.description: As one moves north, Maine's kelp forests are being overtaken by dense mats of carpet-like turf algae. The steady decline of kelp and transition into this new state are altering the ecosystem all the way down to the microbial level, according to a new study in PNAS from Bigelow Laboratory for Ocean Sciences.

phys-org.title: A 112°C test may separate 1,000-year-old pottery from recent forgeries
phys-org.description: Museums around the world now have a new tool to distinguish real ancient clay artifacts from fakes. The research team at UC San Diego's Scripps Institution of Oceanography, led by postdoctoral scholar Yoav Vaknin, found a way to distinguish the magnetism that clay materials acquire over time from the magnetism they acquired the day they were made.

phys-org.title: Scientists put algae to work making fuel. AI reveals which cells are pulling their weight
phys-org.description: Algae have a habit of turning up where they're not wanted. They coat your swimming pool in green gunk, cling to rocks at the beach and even make headlines when they take over prominent reservoirs, such as the White House Reflection Pool. But put them to work in the right setting, and algae can be surprisingly useful. In fact, these plant-like organisms may hold the key to sustainable fuels of the future.

phys-org.title: Researchers make non-recyclable flame-retardant EV composites recyclable
phys-org.description: Korean researchers have developed a recyclable flame-retardant composite that overcomes a fundamental limitation of conventional flame-retardant composites, which cannot be recycled once cured, while maintaining excellent flame resistance.

phys-org.title: Beyond flood maps: Puerto Rico residents seek climate tools built around local needs
phys-org.description: Resources such as sea level rise viewers, heat maps and flood prediction services are crucial tools in a changing climate. NASA Earth Observations (NASA EO) datasets provide important information on these and other natural hazards, but many communities that may benefit from these tools face barriers to accessing them.

phys-org.title: Protecting the peanut: Sensors help fend off fungus
phys-org.description: Sweet, salty, crunchy or creamy—no matter how it's munched, the Virginia peanut has been a cash crop for the commonwealth for much of the past two centuries. But a fungal disease called Sclerotinia blight has decimated peanut plant populations in recent years, with severe outbreaks causing up to a 50% yield loss.

phys-org.title: Wildfire losses have lasting economic consequences for homeowners
phys-org.description: A new National Bureau of Economic Research working paper from the University of California San Diego shows that wildfire damage can have long-term economic consequences for households, resulting in income losses, resident relocation and slow rebuilding for several years after a fire.

phys-org.title: Deadly virus stalks South Africa's sardines
phys-org.description: The tide came in last week carrying thousands of dead sardines onto South Africa's south coast, and by dawn, stretches of Gqeberha's shoreline were flecked with silver.

phys-org.title: Using AI to track bird migration
phys-org.description: On hearing the first cuckoo of spring, the poet's heart might sing, and while one swallow does not make a summer, the annual migrations of bird species across continents have fascinated us for centuries. Today, however, technology is giving ornithologists the means to follow these incredible journeys in ways that would have been unimaginable to earlier generations of naturalists.

phys-org.title: Smoky off-flavors in cocoa aren't caused solely by smoke
phys-org.description: Fermented cocoa occasionally exhibits off-flavors that can compromise the quality of chocolate and other cocoa products. But what causes these undesirable flavors? Researchers at the Leibniz Institute for Food Systems Biology at the Technical University of Munich have now shown that overfermentation of cocoa beans can cause smoky, leathery and cheesy off-flavors. Smoky flavors, therefore, are not necessarily attributable to smoke contamination.

phys-org.title: Malaysia's Sarawak eyes cloud seeding as haze worsens
phys-org.description: Malaysia's Sarawak state plans cloud-seeding operations in early September, officials said Monday, as smoke from fires in neighboring Indonesia pushes air quality to hazardous levels.

phys-org.title: Plant hormones may offer a way to balance crop yield and disease resistance
phys-org.description: Growth or immune response? Higher organisms must constantly balance these two priorities. As in humans, hormones regulate this balance in plants. Researchers at the Technical University of Munich (TUM) have discovered a mechanism by which plant steroid hormones can inhibit immune responses and thereby make resources available for growth.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

proj-syn.description: Economists widely agree that AI will boost labor productivity. proj-syn.title: Latin America's Crime Tax

proj-syn.title: Are The Walls Closing in on Bessent?
proj-syn.description: Far from suggesting financial Armageddon, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s futile efforts to keep a lid on Treasury yields suggest that, once again, the dollar is America’s currency, but everyone else’s problem. But while investors have few alternatives, the bond-salesman-in-chief cannot be complacent.

proj-syn.title: AI Is Reviving Chinese Marxist Economics
proj-syn.description: As recently as two years ago, most Chinese economists paid only lip service to Marxism and assigned Western textbooks to their students. The advent of AI has changed that, because the technology—open source and available to the smallest manufacturer for a pittance—promises to avoid the “rent trap” common to capitalist economies.

proj-syn.title: Gen Z Is Transforming South Asia
proj-syn.description: Facing diminished economic prospects, many young people see not flawed institutions in need of gradual reform, but predatory systems robbing them of their future. Across South Asia, this sense has animated powerful protest movements, some of which could shape their countries' political trajectories for decades to come.

proj-syn.title: How Britain Can Help Build a Fairer Global Economy
proj-syn.description: With the United Kingdom poised to preside over both the G20 and the G7, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has a unique opportunity to usher in a new internationalism grounded not in military posturing, but in the pursuit of a fairer global economy. But he must abandon his predecessor’s defensive approach.

proj-syn.title: Technocracy Can’t Fix Europe
proj-syn.description: A new private initiative bringing together the crème de la crème of European business, financial, economic, and tech elites could well prove useful in kick-starting European growth and innovation. But first, it must recognize that the problem it hopes to solve is fundamentally political.

proj-syn.title: The Fed and the Treasury Are in Denial
proj-syn.description: For most of the postwar era, the United States has enjoyed a privileged position as an issuer of both sovereign debt and US dollars that always found takers. But the US may no longer be able to rely on stable demand for its debt or its currency, forcing policymakers to face the truth about how financial markets are made.

proj-syn.title: To End Global Hunger, Invest in Rural Communities
proj-syn.description: Even as hunger declines around the world, food insecurity remains prevalent in rural communities. Restoring soil health, expanding access to new technologies, strengthening land rights, and upgrading public infrastructure are essential to boost agricultural productivity and protect rural livelihoods.

proj-syn.title: The Sanctions Illusion
proj-syn.description: Those who defend sweeping financial sanctions against countries like Russia and Iran often claim that popular suffering is a defensible means of pressuring the target government. But while such measures certainly inflict widespread suffering on civilian populations, this rarely translates into political change.

proj-syn.title: Is Monetarism Making a Comeback?
proj-syn.description: After decades on the margins of mainstream economic thinking, monetarism is beginning to re-enter the debate, most notably at the Federal Reserve. To regain credibility, however, monetarists must learn from past mistakes and adapt to the monetary and financial realities of the 21st century.

proj-syn.title: China’s Super-Dam Is Becoming an Upstream Water Bomb
proj-syn.description: The latest evidence suggests that the Chinese scientific establishment understands the dangers of a planned Himalayan dam—the world's largest—more clearly than its political leadership is willing to acknowledge. With the livelihoods of two billion people at stake, the international community needs to weigh in.

proj-syn.title: Europe and the War in Ukraine
proj-syn.description: If Europe remains a mere collection of small states and middle powers, the current period of profound geopolitical and historical change will also mark the end of its role on the world stage. With no end in sight for Russia's war in Ukraine, Europeans must come to grips with reality.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Stand with Canada Against Trump
proj-syn.description: Rather than keeping their heads down as US President Donald Trump wages another trade war with Canada, European leaders must recognize that they could be next. Like Canada, the European Union is a middle power whose future prosperity and security will depend on solidarity with economic peers.

proj-syn.title: Is China Really a Champion of the Global South?
proj-syn.description: The United States is an overextended hegemon, and its decline will continue slowly, as other powers like China assume more global responsibilities. Against this backdrop, China’s efforts to lead the Global South are more about consolidating its power in the current international system than creating a new one that benefits all.

proj-syn.title: The Economist’s Embarrassing Proxy War Over AI Policy
proj-syn.description: The disagreements between the Nobel laureate economist Daron Acemoglu and his opponents are consequential—and so are the opponents. But rather than engage in good faith with Acemoglu's arguments, the venerable British news magazine recently stooped to bibulous calumny by unnamed critics of his work.

proj-syn.title: Democracies Must Get Serious About Industrial Policy
proj-syn.description: For decades, Western governments have ceded the strategic direction of their economies to the market. To dominate the industries of the future, they must learn from their own history and rebuild the institutions, expertise, and discipline that effective industrial policy demands.

proj-syn.title: In the AI Gold Rush, the Cloud Wins
proj-syn.description: Even if the AI investment boom turns out to have been a bubble, the Big Tech companies that have cornered the cloud infrastructure market will emerge as strong as ever, or even stronger. That is why Amazon, Microsoft, and Google are in a league of their own, even compared to other giants like Meta and Nvidia.
